facts.content: Patient experiences loose and watery stools without blood.

facts.content: Assessment is acute gastroenteritis with likely viral or foodborne cause.
facts.source_text: 1) Acute gastroenteritis – 3 days watery diarrhea, LLQ crampy pain, initial vomiting, subjective fever; oral intake maintained; likely viral/foodborne.

facts.content: Prescribed oral rehydration solution such as Dioralyte as directed for hydration.
facts.source_text: Hydration: Oral rehydration solution (e.g., Dioralyte) as directed

facts.content: Advised small frequent fluids and bland/light foods as tolerated.
facts.source_text: Diet: Small frequent fluids; bland/light foods as tolerated

facts.content: Advised Paracetamol 1 g orally every 6 hours as needed, maximum 4 g/day for fever or aches.
facts.source_text: Analgesia/antipyretic: Paracetamol 1 g PO q6h PRN (max 4 g/day) for fever/aches

facts.content: Recommended rest and to take 2-3 days off work.

Patient advised to seek medical attention for worsening dehydration, persistent fever over 38.5°C, bloody stools, severe or worsening abdominal pain, symptoms persisting over 7 days, or inability to tolerate oral intake.
facts.source_text: Return/ED precautions: Worsening dehydration (oliguria, dizziness), persistent fever >38.5°C, bloody stools, severe/worsening abd pain, >7 days symptoms, inability to tolerate PO

facts.content: Patient advised to reassess if not improving in 3-4 days and consider stool studies if symptoms persist or are severe.
facts.source_text: Follow-up: Reassess if not improving in 3–4 days; consider stool studies if persistent or severe symptoms
